subject: Residency & KMS/HSM: retention slab vs seat bundle — counteroffer
messages:
From: Harper Dunn <harper@stellarcare.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@stellarcare.com
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Question on retention pricing and KMS seat amortization

Hi Grace —

Thanks for the call earlier. Procurement asked me to get a written confirmation on a couple of points before we loop legal:

1) Audit log retention — your pricing workbook has a 90/365/730 retention slab. Can you confirm if we can mix slabs across environments (90 days for dev, 365 for prod) or whether retention is billed at the account level only?

2) KMS/HSM economics — we see an "HSM seat" line and a separate "managed KMS" fee. For our budget we’d prefer a blended amortized approach (pay some upfront and reduced recurring). Is Redwood open to amortizing the HSM onboarding cost over 12 months as a credit against the monthly seat fee?

3) Residency surcharge — our EU customers will require EU-only residency for a portion of traffic. Is there a way to set a usage split (US vs EU) on the invoice instead of duplicating the residency surcharge for the full commit?

We’re close to a PO but need those answers and a short SOW (so legal can see the line items). I attached our requested scope and a draft SOW.

Best,
Harper Dunn
Senior Sourcing Manager | StellarCare
procurement@stellarcare.com
Attachments: StellarCare_SOW_draft.pdf
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: Harper Dunn <harper@stellarcare.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 11:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Question on retention pricing and KMS seat amortization

Hi Harper —

Appreciate the clear asks. Quick answers up front, with a follow-up proposal attached:

1) Retention slabs can be applied per-environment. You can mix 90/365/730 across dev/staging/prod. We bill retention as a metered line item by storage class and environment tag (not a single account-wide tier) — so your proposed split is supported.

2) HSM onboarding vs seat fee: we can amortize the onboarding/attestation cost as a one-time credit applied over 12 months against the monthly HSM seat charge. Practically we convert the onboarding into a prepaid credit and consume it each month. I included two variants in the attached workbook: (A) 12-month amortization, (B) 36-month amortization.

3) Residency surcharge: we can invoice residency as a usage allocation. For the initial contract we recommend (a) define primary region mapping, (b) add a usage percentage field to monthly invoices so you only pay residency surcharge on the portion of tokens/embeddings routed to EU pools. That avoids double-charging the full commit.

Attached: Redwood_pricing_workbook_v3.xlsx (variant pricing + example invoice rows) and a short SOW skeleton.

If this matches what procurement needs I’ll loop Ben on the commercial concession and Laura for final approval on any deviations from standard terms. Next steps: confirm which amortization variant you prefer and your target retention per environment.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Lead, Strategic Accounts (Compliance Practice)
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_pricing_workbook_v3.xlsx
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Harper Dunn <harper@stellarcare.com>, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 09:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on retention pricing and KMS seat amortization

Hi Harper —

Looping in on the commercial side. We did the math on Redwood_pricing_workbook_v3 and here’s a pragmatic counter we can live with while keeping program economics intact:

- HSM onboarding amortization: we’ll offer the 12-month amortization but with a 30% upfront payment to be applied as immediate credit, then the remaining 70% will be spread equally over 11 months. This reduces our credit exposure if the contract terminates early.
- Residency surcharge: we’ll accept a usage-split invoicing approach but to be fair to our capacity planning we need a committed minimum for EU-resident throughput (suggest 20% of committed tokens for year 1). If actual EU usage exceeds the minimum we’ll bill monthly overage; if it's below we’ll rebate the difference quarterly.
- Retention: ok to mix slabs per environment. For the prod 365 slab we can provide a 15% discount on storage cost if you commit to a 12-month retention minimum for prod environments.

If StellarCare can accept the upfront fraction on onboarding and the 20% EU minimum, we can take this to Legal and issue a redline-ready SOW + PO template. If not, indicate which element you’d like to trade (e.g., higher upfront, lower minimum, longer amortization).

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Director, Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference
From: Harper Dunn <harper@stellarcare.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@stellarcare.com
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on retention pricing and KMS seat amortization

Ben / Grace —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the workbook. Procurement and finance discussed your counter offline. We can accept the 12-month amortization structure with the 30% upfront payment and the 70% spread over the remaining months. We also agree to the 20% EU committed throughput minimum for year 1. The 15% discount on 365 prod storage for a 12-month retention minimum is acceptable.

Next ask: please send the redline-ready SOW and a draft PO line items (we’ll need the invoice-friendly descriptions) and I’ll circulate to legal and our finance approver this afternoon.

We’ve attached an updated scope PDF with token estimates per environment — please confirm the final invoice rows so we can lock the PO.

Appreciate the help, looking forward to getting this over the finish line.

Best,
Harper Dunn
Senior Sourcing Manager | StellarCare
attachments: StellarCare_SOW_draft_v2.pdf
